ce:2001:q1.question: The number of boundary conditions required to solve the differential equation $\frac{\partial^2 \phi }{\partial x^2}+\frac{\partial^2 \phi }{\partial y^2}=0$ is

detailed_solution.concept: CE Core Engineering
Engineering Mathematics - Ordinary Differential Equation
detailed_solution.markdown:
$$\begin{aligned} I&=\int_{0}^{\pi /4}\cos ^{2}xdx \\  &=\int_{0}^{\pi /4}\frac{1+\cos 2x}{2}dx \\  &=\int_{0}^{\pi /4}\frac{dX}{2}+\int_{0}^{\pi /4}\frac{\cos 2x}{2}dx \\  &=\frac{1}{2}\left [ x \right ]_{0}^{\pi /4}+\frac{1}{2}\left [ \frac{\sin 2x}{2} \right ]_{0}^{\pi /4} \\  &=\frac{\pi }{8}+\frac{1}{4}\left [ \sin \frac{\pi }{2}-\sin x \right ] \\  &=\frac{\pi }{8}+\frac{1}{4}\times 1 =\frac{\pi }{8}+\frac{1}{4} \end{aligned}$$

Therefore, the correct answer is **A**.

ce:2001:q4.title: GATE CE 2001 | Set 1 | Question: 4
ce:2001:q4.question: The degree of static indeterminacy, $N_s$, and the degree of kinematic indeterminacy, $N_k$ , for the plane frame shown below, assuming axial deformations to be negligible, are given by

detailed_solution.concept: Structural Analysis - Determinacy and Indeterminacy
detailed_solution.markdown:
Degree of static indeterminacy,

$$\begin{aligned} N_{s} &=3 m+r_{e}-3 j-r_{r} \\ &=3 \times 5+(3+2+2)-3 \times 6-0 \\ &=4 \end{aligned}$$

Degree of kinematic indeterminacy,

$$\begin{aligned} N_{k} &=3 j-r_{e}-m \\ &=3 \times 6-(3+2+2)-5=6 \\ N_{s} &=4 \text { and } N_{k}=6 \end{aligned}$$

Therefore, the correct answer is **C**.

ce:2001:q12.question:
The following two statements are made with reference to the calculation of net bearing capacity of a footing in pure clay soil ($\phi =0$) using Terzaghi's bearing capacity theory. Identify if they are TRUE or FALSE.

I. Increase in footing width will result in increase in bearing capacity.
II. Increase in depth of foundation will result in higher bearing capacity.
options: I is TRUE but II is FALSE
II is TRUE but I is FALSE

detailed_solution.concept: Geotechnical Engineering - Shallow Foundation and Bearing Capacity
detailed_solution.markdown:
$q_{u}=c N_{c}+\gamma D_{i} N_{q}+0.5 \gamma B N_{\gamma}$

For pure clay,

$$\begin{aligned} \phi &=0, N_{c}=5.7, N_{q}=1, N_{\gamma}=0 \\ \therefore \quad a_{u} &=c N_{c}+\gamma D_{t} \\ q_{n u} &=c N_{c}+\gamma D_{t}-\gamma D_{t}=c N_{c} \end{aligned}$$

Therefore, the correct answer is **B**.

ce:2001:q28.title: GATE CE 2001 | Set 1 | Question: 28
ce:2001:q28.question:
The solution for the following differential equation with boundary conditions y(0)=2 and y'(1)=-3 is
$\frac{d^{2}y}{dx^{2}}=3x-2$

detailed_solution.concept: Engineering Mathematics - Ordinary Differential Equation
detailed_solution.markdown:
$\frac{dy}{dx} = \frac{3x^{2}}{2}-2x+C_{1}$

Integrating, we get,

$$\begin{aligned}  y&=\frac{3x^{3}}{6}-\frac{2x^{2}}{2}+C_{1}x+C_{2} \\ \therefore  \;\; y\left ( 0 \right )&=2=0+10+C_{2} \\  C_{2}&=2\\ \text{Again }  -3&=\frac{3}{2}\left ( 1 \right )^{2}-2\left ( 1 \right )+C_{1} \\  -3&=1.5-2+C_{1}\\ C_{1}&=-3+0.5 \\&=-2.5=-\frac{5}{2} \\   y&=\frac{x^{3}}{2}-x^{2}-\frac{5}{2}x+2\end{aligned}$$

Therefore, the correct answer is **C**.

ce:2001:q29.question:

Therefore, the correct answer is **A**.

ce:2001:q30.title: GATE CE 2001 | Set 1 | Question: 30
ce:2001:q30.question: The Eigen values of the matrix $$\begin{bmatrix} 5 &3 \\ 2& 9 \end{bmatrix}$$ are

detailed_solution.concept: Engineering Mathematics - Linear Algebra
detailed_solution.markdown:
$$\begin{bmatrix} 5-\lambda & 3\\ 2 & 9-\lambda \end{bmatrix}=0$$

or $\left ( 5-\lambda \right )\left ( 9-\lambda \right )-6=0$

or $45-9\lambda -5\lambda +\lambda ^{2}-6=0$

or $\lambda ^{2}-14\lambda +39=0$

solving we get,

$\lambda =10.1623,\, 3.837$

Hence eigen value of the matrix are $(10.16, 3.837)$

Therefore, the correct answer is **D**.

ce:2001:q31.title: GATE CE 2001 | Set 1 | Question: 31
ce:2001:q31.question: The frame below shows three beam elements OA, OB and OC, with identical length L and flexural rigidity El , subject to an external moment M applied at the rigid joint O. The correct set of bending moments $\{M_{OA},M_{OB},M_{OC}\}$, that develop at O in the three beam elements OA, OB and OC respectively, is

detailed_solution.concept: Structural Analysis - Methods of Structural Analysis
detailed_solution.markdown: $$\begin{aligned} M_{O A} &=M \times D F \text { for } O A \\ &=M \times \frac{3}{7}=\frac{3}{7} M\\ M_{O B} &=0 \\ M_{O C} &=M \times D F \text { for } O C \\ &=M \times \frac{4}{7}=\frac{4}{7} M \end{aligned}$$ Therefore, the correct answer is **D**.

ce:2001:q32.title: GATE CE 2001 | Set 1 | Question: 32
ce:2001:q32.question: Identify, from the following, the correct value of the bending moment $M_A$ (in kNm units) at the fixed end A in the statically determinate beam shown below (with internal hinges at B and D), when a uniformly distributed load of 10 kN/m is placed on all spans. (Hint: Sketching the influence line for $M_A$ or applying the Principle of Virtual Displacements makes the solution easy).

primary.subtopicLabel: Influence Line Diagram and Rolling Loads

detailed_solution.concept: Structural Analysis - Influence Line Diagram and Rolling Loads
detailed_solution.markdown: ILD for BM at A by using Muller Breslau principle will be $$\begin{aligned} M_{A}&=\text { Net area of } 1 L D \times 10 \\ M_{A}&=\left[-\left(\frac{1}{2} \times 2 \times 4\right)+\left(\frac{1}{2} \times 2 \times 4\right)\right] \times 10=0 \mathrm{kNm} \end{aligned}$$ Therefore, the correct answer is **C**.

ce:2001:q33.title: GATE CE 2001 | Set 1 | Question: 33
ce:2001:q33.question: The end moment (in kNm units) developed in the roof level beams in the laterally loaded frame shown below (with all columns having identical cross-sections) according to the Cantilever Method of simplified analysis, is

detailed_solution.concept: Structural Analysis - Methods of Structural Analysis
detailed_solution.markdown: According to cantilever method, point of contraflexure lies at mid point of each span and direct stresses (axial) in column due to horizontal forces are directly proportional to their distance from the centroidal vertical axis of frame. $\overline{h}$ = CG of frame will be at mid column due to symmetry. $\overline{h}=\frac{1\times0+2\times6+1\times12}{3}=6m$ Since, areas of each column are equal so axial force in each column will be in proportional to their distance from CG . $\frac{V_{1}}{x_{1}}=\frac{V_{3}}{x_{3}}$ As distance of $V_{2}$ from C G=0 $\therefore \quad V_{2}=0$ $$\begin{aligned} \frac{V_{1}}{6}&=\frac{V_{3}}{6}\\ \Rightarrow \quad V_{1}&=V_{3} \end{aligned}$$ Take moment about L $$\begin{aligned} 30 \times 2 &=V_{1} \times 12 \\ V_{1} &=5 \mathrm{kN} \end{aligned}$$ and from equilibrium of forces end moment at roof level beam $=7.5 \times 2=15 \mathrm{kNm}$ Therefore, the correct answer is **B**.

ce:2001:q34.title: GATE CE 2001 | Set 1 | Question: 34
ce:2001:q34.question:
Consider the following two statements related to reinforced concrete design, and identify whether they are TRUE of FALSE:

I. Curtailment of bars in the flexural tension zone in beams reduces the shear strength at the cut-off locations.
II. When a rectangular column section is subject to biaxially eccentric compression, the neutral axis will be parallel to the resultant axis of bending.
options: Both statements I and II are TRUE
Statement I is TRUE, and statement II is FALSE
Statement I is FALSE, and statement II is TRUE
Both Statements I and II are FALSE

primary.subtopicLabel: Shear, Torsion, Bond, Anchorage and Development Length

detailed_solution.concept: RCC Structures - Shear, Torsion, Bond, Anchorage and Development Length
detailed_solution.markdown: Statement I: Curtailment of bars in the flexural tension zone in beams reduces the shear strength at the cut-off locations. This statement is TRUE because cutting tensile reinforcement decreases dowel action and reduces shear resistance at that location. Statement II: When a rectangular column is subjected to biaxially eccentric compression, the neutral axis will be parallel to the resultant axis of bending. This statement is FALSE because for biaxial bending, the neutral axis is governed by the interaction: $M_x y + M_y x = 0$ The slope of the neutral axis is: $\text{slope of N.A.} = -\frac{M_y}{M_x}$ Whereas the resultant bending axis has slope: $\text{slope of resultant moment axis} =\frac{M_y}{M_x}$ Thus, they are not parallel. Therefore, the correct answer is **B**.

Therefore, the correct answer is **D**.

ce:2001:q38.title: GATE CE 2001 | Set 1 | Question: 38
ce:2001:q38.question:
The coefficients of permeability of a soil in horizontal and vertical directions are
3.46 and 1.5 m/day respectively. The base length of a concrete dam resting in this soil is 100 m. When the flow net is developed for this soil with 1:25 scale factor in the vertical direction, the reduced base length of the dam will be

detailed_solution.concept: Geotechnical Engineering - Effective Stress and Permeability
detailed_solution.markdown:
$$\begin{aligned} K_{x}&=3.46 \mathrm{m} / \mathrm{day} \\ K_{y}&=1.5 \mathrm{m} / \mathrm{day} l_{b}&=100 \mathrm{m} \text{(base length)}\\ \end{aligned}$$

scale factor in vertical direction =1: 25

scale factor in horizontal direction

$=\frac{1}{25} \sqrt{\frac{K_{y}}{K_{x}}}=\frac{1}{37.969}$

$\therefore$ Reduced base length = scale $\times l_{\mathrm{b}}$

$=\frac{100}{37.969}=2.63 \mathrm{m}$

Therefore, the correct answer is **A**.

ce:2001:q43.title: GATE CE 2001 | Set 1 | Question: 43
ce:2001:q43.question: A field was supplied water from an irrigation tank at a rate of 120 lit/sec to irrigate an area of 2.5 hectares. The duration of irrigation is 8 hours. It was found that the actual delivery at the field, which is about 4 km from the tank, was 100 lit/sec. The runoff loss in the field was estimated as 800 $m^3$. The application efficiency in this situation is

detailed_solution.concept: Irrigation Engineering - Crop Water Requirements
detailed_solution.markdown:
Water application efficiency,

$$\eta_{\mathrm{a}}=\frac{\begin{array}{c}\text{Water stored in the}\\ \text { root zone during irrigation }\end{array}}{\text { Water delivered to the field }} \times 100$$

Water supplied to field during 8 hour @ 100 lit/s

$$\begin{array}{l} =100 \times 8 \times 60 \times 60 \\ =2880 \mathrm{m}^{3} \end{array}$$

Runoff loss in the field $=800 \mathrm{m}^{3}$

Water stored in the root zone

$$\begin{aligned} &=2880-800=2080 \mathrm{m}^{3} \\ \therefore \quad \eta_{\mathrm{a}}&=\frac{2080}{2880} \times 100=72.22 \% \end{aligned}$$

Therefore, the correct answer is **B**.

ce:2001:q44.title: GATE CE 2001 | Set 1 | Question: 44
ce:2001:q44.question: A trapezoidal channel with bottom width of 3 m and side slope of IV:1.5H carries a discharge of 8.0 $m^3/sec$ with the flow depth of 1.5 m. The Froude number of the flow is

detailed_solution.concept: Fluid Mechanics and Hydraulics - Open Channel Flow
detailed_solution.markdown: $$\begin{aligned} Q&=8 \mathrm{m}^{3} / \mathrm{s} \\ A&=\frac{1}{2}(3+7.5) \times 1.5=7.875 \mathrm{m}^{2} \\ V&=\frac{Q}{\mathrm{A}}=\frac{8}{7.875}=1.015 \mathrm{m} / \mathrm{s}\\ \text{Now}\quad \frac{1}{1.5}&=\frac{1.5}{x} \\ x&=2.25\\ T&=3+2 \times 2.25=7.5 \mathrm{m} \\ D&=\frac{A}{T}=\frac{7.875}{7.5}=1.05 \\ F&=\frac{V}{\sqrt{\mathrm{g} \mathrm{D}}}=\frac{1.05}{\sqrt{9.81 \times 1.05}}=0.316 \end{aligned}$$ Hence no any option is correct. Therefore, the correct answer is **D**.

ce:2001:q45.title: GATE CE 2001 | Set 1 | Question: 45
ce:2001:q45.question: In a 1/50 model of a spillway, the discharge was measured to be 0.3 $m^{3}/sec$. The corresponding prototype discharge in $m^{3}/sec$ is

detailed_solution.concept: Fluid Mechanics and Hydraulics - Dimensional Analysis
detailed_solution.markdown:
$$\begin{aligned} Q_{r} &=L_{r}^{25} \\ \frac{Q_{\mathrm{p}}}{Q_{m}} &=\left(\frac{L_{p}}{L_{m}}\right)^{25}(50)^{25} \\ \therefore \quad Q_{p} &=0.3 \times(50)^{25}=5303.3 \mathrm{m}^{3 / \mathrm{s}} \end{aligned}$$

Therefore, the correct answer is **D**.

ce:2001:q46.title: GATE CE 2001 | Set 1 | Question: 46
ce:2001:q46.question: If the $BOD_{5,20}$ of waste is 150 mg/L and the reaction rate constant (to the base 'e') at 20$^{\circ}$C is 0.35/day, the ultimate BOD in mg/L is

primary.subtopicLabel: Quality and Characteristics of Waste Water

detailed_solution.concept: Environmental Engineering - Quality and Characteristics of Waste Water
detailed_solution.markdown:
$$\begin{aligned} k_{D} &=\frac{0.35}{2.3}=0.15/days \\ \text{Now}\; \;150 &=L\left [ 1-10^{-0.15\times 5} \right ]=0.822\: l \\ \therefore \; \; L &=\frac{150}{0.822}=181.54\: mg/l \end{aligned}$$

Therefore, the correct answer is **B**.

ce:2001:q47.title: GATE CE 2001 | Set 1 | Question: 47
ce:2001:q47.question: The $Ca^{2+}$ concentration and $Mg^{2+}$ concentration of a water sample are 160 mg/lit and 40 mg/lit as their ions respectively. The total hardness of this water sample in terms of $CaCO_3$ in mg/lit is approximately equal to

detailed_solution.concept: Environmental Engineering - Quality Characteristics of Water
detailed_solution.markdown:
Total hardness

$$\begin{aligned} &=Ca^{+}\: mg/l\left ( \frac{50}{20} \right )+Mg^{+}\: mg/l\times \left ( \frac{50}{12} \right ) \\ &=160\times \frac{50}{20}+40\times \frac{50}{12} \\ &=566.67\: mg/l \end{aligned}$$

Therefore, the correct answer is **D**.

ce:2001:q48.title: GATE CE 2001 | Set 1 | Question: 48
ce:2001:q48.question: A town has an existing horizontal flow sedimentation tank with an overflow rate of 17 $m^3/day/m^2$, and it is desirable to remove particles that have settling velocity of 0.1 mm/sec. Assuming the tank is an ideal sedimentation tank, the percentage of particles removal is approximately equal to

detailed_solution.concept: Environmental Engineering - Water Treatment
detailed_solution.markdown:
$$\begin{aligned} \text{Overflow rate} &=17\; m^{3}/day/m^{2} \\ &=17\; m/day \\ &=\frac{17\times 1000}{24\times 60\times 60} \\ &=0.196\; mm/s \end{aligned}$$

Percentage particle removal

$$\begin{aligned} &=\frac{0.1}{0.196}\times 100=50\% \end{aligned}$$

Therefore, the correct answer is **B**.

ce:2001:q49.title: GATE CE 2001 | Set 1 | Question: 49
ce:2001:q49.question: A valley curve has a descending gradient of 1 in 40 followed by an ascending gradient of 1 in 50. The length of the valley curve required for a design speed of 80 km/hour for comfort condition is

primary.subtopicLabel: Geometric Design of Highway and Planning

detailed_solution.concept: Transportation Engineering - Geometric Design of Highway and Planning
detailed_solution.markdown:
$$\begin{aligned} L &=2\left[\frac{N v^{3}}{C}\right]^{1 / 2} \\ &=0.38\left[N V^{8}\right]^{1 / 2} \quad\left[\text { since } C=0.6 \mathrm{m} / \mathrm{s}^{3}\right] \\ N &=\frac{1}{40}-\left(+\frac{1}{50}\right)=\frac{1}{40}+\frac{1}{50}=0.045 \\ \therefore \quad L &=0.38\left[0.045 \times 80^{3}\right]^{1 / 2} \\ &=57.67 \mathrm{m} \simeq 58 \mathrm{m} \end{aligned}$$

Therefore, the correct answer is **C**.

ce:2001:q50.title: GATE CE 2001 | Set 1 | Question: 50
ce:2001:q50.question: The radius of relatives stiffness for a 20 cm thick slab with $E = 3 \times 10^{5} kg/cm^{2}$ and poisson's ratio = 0.15, resting on a subgrade having modulus of 5 kg/$cm^{3}$ is

detailed_solution.concept: Transportation Engineering - Pavement Design
detailed_solution.markdown:
$$\begin{array}{l} \text { Given, } h=20 \mathrm{cm}, E=3 \times 10^{5} \mathrm{kg} / \mathrm{cm}^{2} \\ \mu=0.15, k=5 \mathrm{kg} / \mathrm{cm}^{3} \\ \qquad \begin{aligned} L &=\left[\frac{E h^{3}}{12 k\left(1-\mu^{2}\right)}\right]^{1 / 4} \\ &=\left[\frac{3 \times 10^{5} \times 20^{3}}{12 \times 5\left[1-(0.15)^{2}\right]}\right]^{1 / 4}\\ &79.98cm\approx80cm \end{aligned} \end{array}$$

Therefore, the correct answer is **B**.
